evidence.quote: Potential impacts included in our Paris Ambition (1.5°C) scenario analysis included the following (the ‘No Policy’ (4°C) scenario was not relevant): — Direct increase to overhead costs from Scope 1 and 2 emissions (e.g. cost of electricity and fuel). — Increased cost of raw materials from upstream suppliers passing through increased costs from Scope 3 emissions. — Reduction in sales from passing the costs from carbon taxes on to consumers. — Under a Paris Ambition (1.5°C) scenario global carbon prices are expected to grow in the medium term. Failure to achieve our SBTi-aligned target for Scope 1 and 2 emissions can lead to a medium risk. However, if we meet our SBTi target, the risk is significantly reduced as we aim to achieve at least 95% absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions reduction by 2030 (vs a 2020 baseline). — Indirect Scope 3 emissions account for the majority of our exposure to carbon costs, particularly upstream emissions associated with farming and processing, which could be passed on by our suppliers.
